item.title: Remembering Shirley Muldowney
item.description: SHE'S STILL ALIVE , titles can't be edited... Shirley Muldowney is retired from professional racing and remains active in the drag racing community at 86 years old, frequently making public appearances and supporting her nonprofit charity. Shirley Muldowney didn't just race Top Fuel dragsters — she flat out dominated them, and she did it in a sport that didn't want her anywhere near the starting line. Back in the late '60s, guys refused to race her, sneered at her, questioned whether a woman should even be allowed near a nitro-burning car. Muldowney didn't argue back. She just kept winning. Three world championships — 1977, 1980, 1982 — eighteen national event wins, and she's still the only woman to ever win the U.S. Nationals, drag racing's biggest race of all. Then came Montreal, 1984. Her car came apart at 250 mph. She was pulled from the wreck with every finger broken, her pelvis shattered, both legs mangled. Doctors weren't sure she'd walk again, let alone race. It took five surgeries and eighteen months just to relearn how to grip a steering wheel. She came back anyway. Not for a photo op — to race, in the same 280 mph class that nearly killed her. In 1989, at 49 years old, she ran a 4.97-second pass and became the first driver ever to break the five-second barrier three races in a row. They made a movie about her — "Heart Like a Wheel," with Bonnie Bedelia — but it came out a year before the crash. So the film never even got to the hardest part of her story: crawling back from a wreck that should've ended everything, and proving she was faster than ever. Muldowney's in the Motorsports Hall of Fame now. But the real legacy is simpler than any trophy: she showed up, she strapped in, and she ran numbers nobody could argue with.

item.title: GovBrief Today #588
item.description: It took the US Supreme Court to make Missouri count 305,000 of its own voters' signatures. They filed a petition in December protesting a map that carved up a Democratic seat in Kansas City at Donald Trump's urging. Missouri's secretary of state sat on it for eight months, then rejected it on primary day. When Missouri's own Supreme Court ruled the new map illegal, a federal judge in St. Louis ordered him to use it anyway, and he told every county election official the federal order came first. Today the US Supreme Court insisted, without a single dissent, that the old map be used. Then Missouri's Supreme Court called Secretary of State Denny Hoskins in and found him in contempt for ignoring its order. Missouri will now vote in November on the lines that already existed. item.title: I'm doing okay but was just checking
item.description:
I am doing okay 'ish still but I always like to have ideas on what to do for extra income just in case I still can't find a job. I had checked once a plasma place a few years ago who said I didn't qualify but thought I'd try my luck again out of curiosity and second opinion. I still don't qualify. Tiny veins even when hydrated and they said with my chronic issues too even if I did pass the screening somewhere it is taxing and takes hours.
I have applied to many places but Burlington just pissing me off with their repetative AI responses and no interview!
I started deleting their emails and finally just unsubscribed. It all said THE SAME THING. I AM STILL WAITING FOR AN INTERVIEW OPENING.
They even texted me the same thing for days over and over.
I am a bit stressed about finding a job already cause I need insurance even Medicaid but it requires proof of working at least 80 hours a month to qualify. I am trying and applying. I know something is out there for me! I am keeping positive and motivated because there is no use crumbling when I already am doing better being back home away from my husband and that prison of lies and betrayal. I just gotta vent. Thank you for listening.
Speaking of positive, I had my first try at the gym today. My god have I gotten so week and squishy since being sedentary for months stuck in France. I did the best I could with my arms and on a bike. I always have a hard time working out even when I am my most "physically fit" which makes me laugh to say cause my MCAS and other health issues just make it so much harder to exercise, but I took breaks to catch my breath and slow my dizzy spells. I felt good leaving the gym and feel pumped to keep going and getting healthier and stronger. I also asked if they were hiring but they said no :( It's okay, there is something out there for me!
Saw this car in front of me today too. It was a nice sign. I hope something good happens to you all and may you all have a lovely rest of your weekend.
